reader.requirement: At --std 85 an indexed file's file-name may appear in only one SELECT of a program's FILE-CONTROL paragraph, and every file-name a SELECT names must have an FD in the Data Division of the same program (a SELECT in a containing program is not satisfied by an FD in a contained one).
reader.edition-search: Read BindFileControl (SelectedFiles duplicate check, COBOL2634) and ScreenSelectsHaveDescriptions (COBOL2635): neither reads Edition.DialectLevel, CobolVersion, ConstructRegistry or ReservedWords; EditionContext.Error (EditionContext.cs#Error) only records the diagnostic. The only DialectLevel reads in BindFileControl are on the PADDING clause, not on this path.
reader.witnesses-cover: part: the witnesses exercise the per-program scope with sequential files and the FD-without-SELECT direction; none exercises a duplicate SELECT or a SELECT without FD on an INDEXED file at 85 (probed here).

reader.notes: Both sentences are enforced edition-invariantly by the two binder screens; the 2023 rule (§2023:12.4.5.2 SR2/SR3) states the same obligation, so one arm serves every edition. The diagnostics cite the 2023 clause even at --std 85, a cosmetic point only.

refuter.evidence: Probe r1nest.cob (refute-1985-046/r1nest-001, --std 85): a containing and a contained program each with its own SELECT IX (indexed, DYNAMIC) and its own FD IX compiles and runs, IN=ZZZZ999999 OUT=AAAA111111, exit 0: the once-only rule is per program, not per run unit, as SR2 reads ('in the Data Division of the same program'). The reader's c1dup/c1nofd/c1nested already show the two refusals (COBOL2634, COBOL2635/2636).
